LESSON: READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: (NARRATIVE OF ABOUT 400 WORDS)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words), part of Strand 3 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do you get information from a text? 2. Which things do you predict or visualize in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. relate events in the story with their life experiences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. predict events in a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create mental images from the events in a story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. respond to factual and inferential questions correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. relate events in a reading text to real life experiences.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. relate events in the story with their life experiences,

   Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. predict events in a text for comprehension,

   Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. create mental images from the events in a story,

   Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. respond to factual and inferential questions correctly,

   Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. relate events in a reading text to real life experiences.

   Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. make predictions on a story

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. make predictions on a story

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: (Narrative of about 400 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy is developed as the learner predicts and visualises stories from texts.

• Communication is enhanced as the learner works with peers to scan and skim the text and share information

20

Values:
Social justice is promoted as the learner uses their imagination to visualise the events in a story

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education: The learner acquires the skills of living with others from reading texts on etiquette especially

table manners.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link the content derived from the theme of etiquette to what is learnt in Agriculture.

Main points to remember:

1. relate events in the story with their life experiences,
2. predict events in a text for comprehension,
3. create mental images from the events in a story,
4. respond to factual and inferential questions correctly,
5. relate events in a reading text to real life experiences.
